title: Theoretical probability
goal: I can calculate probability from equally likely outcomes.
teach: When all the outcomes are equally likely, P(event) = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of outcomes. For example, an ordinary dice has 6 equally likely outcomes, so P(4) = ⅙.
tvis: 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green counters: 10 altogether.

ex.q: One counter is taken without looking from the bag in Teach. Find P(blue).

watch:
Count the counters, not the colours.

Problem-solving lens
Write the fraction as “how many I want” over “how many there are”, then simplify.

qs.text: A dice is rolled. Find P(4).
qs.steps:
1. Formula: P(event) = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of equally likely outcomes
2. One 4 out of 6 numbers
3. P(4) = 16

qs.text: A dice is rolled. Find P(a prime number).
qs.steps:
1. Formula: P(event) = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of equally likely outcomes
2. Primes on a dice: 2, 3, 5 (3 numbers)
3. P = 36 = 12

qs.text: One letter of the word MATHEMATICS is chosen at random. Find P(M).
qs.steps:
1. Formula: P(event) = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of equally likely outcomes
2. MATHEMATICS has 11 letters and 2 Ms
3. P(M) = 211
